length.text: Usually under 1 m; the longest males about 1.2 m

reproduction.text: Live young, about 2 to 17 at a time

overview.text: The Mojave (or Mohave) Rattlesnake is a venomous pit viper of the deserts of the south-western United States and Mexico. Many populations have a venom that attacks the nerves, which gave it a reputation as one of the most dangerous rattlesnakes - but people bitten by it do no worse, on average, than people bitten by other rattlesnakes of the same size.

identification.text: It looks very like the Western Diamond-backed Rattlesnake, which lives in the same areas. There is no single sure sign: its colour ranges from green to brown, grey or yellowish, with a row of diamond-shaped blotches down the back.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Most are under 1 m long. The largest recorded male was 123.6 cm and the largest female 92.2 cm.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: South-western USA (southern California, southern Nevada, south-west Utah, Arizona, southern New Mexico and west Texas) and much of northern and central Mexico, south to Puebla.

habitat.text: Broad desert valleys and lower mountain slopes with sparse plants such as creosote bush, mesquite, cacti and Joshua trees; it tends to avoid thick vegetation and very rocky ground.

behaviour.text: Most active from April to September. It does not gather in shared winter dens: each snake keeps its own home range all year and shelters in burrows in winter and in the hottest weather.

behaviour.label: Bites
behaviour.text: Its bite can be life-threatening and needs hospital care; the antivenoms used in the United States are made to work against it.

diet.text: An ambush hunter that waits for prey - mostly small rodents and lizards.

reproduction.text: Courtship starts in late summer, pauses over winter and carries on in spring. Females give birth to live young - 2 to 17, about 8 on average - between July and September.

funfacts.text: Experts still argue about how to spell its name: Mojave or Mohave - both are used.

recognise.text: A row of diamond-shaped blotches down the back.
A rattle on the tail tip.

recognise.label: Colour
recognise.text: Greenish, brown, grey or yellowish - the reason for its nickname 'Mojave green'.
